artifacts.summary: 6-phase, ~9h plan coupling capture.projects[].enabled to sapience-extension activation via two new standalone actions on setup-sapience-mcp.sh, invoked from the existing bidirectional SessionStart hook; includes verifier check (i) update, per-repo-scoping.md rewrite with the folders double-gate caveat, and fixture-HOME tests against a stubbed sapience binary.

memory_candidates.content: A read-side resolution rule is not automatically the right predicate for a write-side idempotence check. When coupling a hook to an external config map, the idempotence decision must compare against the exact state the WRITER keys on, not against whatever resolution rule the READER uses. Concrete case: ~/.sapience/config.json's capture.projects[] is READ by longest-path-prefix match (sapience_capture.py's for_cwd()/match_project()), but sapience_capture.set_project() creates and matches an entry by exact string-equal realpath'd path_prefix. Deciding 'already in the desired state, skip the call' from the longest-prefix match would make a child repo sitting under an enabled parent prefix never acquire its own entry, so the coupling silently never fires for it. Generalization: before writing an idempotence guard against external state, identify the writer's own key predicate separately from the reader's, and guard on the writer's.
